newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt asks neighbours to keep out of north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Egypt asks neighbours to keep out of north Iraq.

text.p: Egypt asked Iraq's neighbours on Thursday to stay out of Iraqi affairs and refrain from trying to exploit events in Iraqi Kurdistan, where one Kurdish faction close to Iran has gone on the offensive against its rival.

"Egypt is following with grave concern developments in the situation in northern Iraq and its military repercussions, which threaten the independence and territorial integrity of Iraq," a foreign ministry statement said.

"Egypt again calls on all neighbouring states to respect Iraqi sovereignty and territorial integrity and not to interfere in its internal affairs or exploit current circumstances to achieve transient interests," it added, quoting a spokesman.
The statement did not mention Iran by name but diplomats in Cairo say anxiety about Iranian intentions is an important element in Egypt's opposition to any fragmentation of Iraq.

In Baghdad on Wednesday, Iraqi Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi accused Iran of meddling in northern Iraq and urged Tehran to keep out of fighting between the rival Kurdish factions.

Massoud Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), has said that Iranian forces entered northern Iraq to help rival guerrillas of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) retake a key city last Sunday. Iran and the PUK deny this.
On Thursday Barzani said he might ask Baghdad for help against the PUK, as he did during an offensive last month.
